newsitem.title: ZAIRE: U.N. special envoy arrives to talk to Kabila.
newsitem.headline: U.N. special envoy arrives to talk to Kabila.

text.p: United Nations special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun arrived in Lubumbashi on Sunday to meet the leaders of Zaire's rebel alliance, the day after they took control of the capital Kinshasa.
"My mission is to meet with the leaders of the Alliance and President Kabila and discuss the future of Zaire," he said on arrival at the airport.

Sahnoun, accompanied by a special representative of the Organisation of African Unity, Mamadou Kamme, arrived as a delegation of Alliance leaders prepared to leave for Kinshasa to reassure the capital city's population about security.

Asked what he thought about the change of government, Sahnoun said: "I think it is the wish of the people and that is clear from the fact that in Kinshasa we have not seen any bloodshed or any grave incident."

Bizimah Karah, the "foreign minister" of the rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo (AFDL), said South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki was due to arrive in Lubumbashi at 4 p.m. (1500 GMT).
The 30-strong Alliance delegation to Kinshasa, led by Deogratius Bugera, Alliance Secretary-General, was assembled at the airport after an earlier delay caused by a shortage of aviation fuel.

Delegation member Letya Mussa Nyembo said it was not part of the mission's mandate to start negotiations with Kinshasa's politicians on forming a government, but merely to "see how to run Kinshasa administratively, how to occupy the city and run it".
